ops.title: call_cli's lazy spawnllm import is shadowed by the session's CWD, crashing every hook that calls it inside a same-named repo
ops.description:
`ContextAPI.call_cli` lazily imports `spawnllm.proc` at call time. When a hook fires in a session whose CWD is a repo that itself provides a top-level package of the same name, Python resolves the import against the **working tree** instead of captain_hook's venv. If that working tree has dependencies the capt-hook venv lacks, every hook that routes through `call_cli` dies.

Observed on yasyf's Mac, 2026-07-25/26, repeatedly (27 occurrences; a burst at 01:45-01:47 on 07-26).

## The chain

    captain_hook/dispatch.py:32                 in run_handler
    codex 1.5.0 agent_plane.py:23               in agent_inject
    codex 1.5.0 common.py:26                    in call_bin
    captain_hook/context.py:135                 in call_cli
        from spawnllm.proc import run_cli
    /Users/yasyf/Code/spawnllm/spawnllm/__init__.py:12
    /Users/yasyf/Code/spawnllm/spawnllm/backends/__init__.py:5
    /Users/yasyf/Code/spawnllm/spawnllm/backends/base.py:24
        from spawnllm import _core
    /Users/yasyf/Code/spawnllm/spawnllm/_core/__init__.py:23
        from wasmtime import Engine, Func, Linker, Memory, Module, Store, Trap, WasiConfig, WasmtimeError

    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'wasmtime'

## The load-bearing detail

The resolved paths are `/Users/yasyf/Code/spawnllm/...`, **not** the `spawnllm` installed in the capt-hook venv. Two checks confirm the venv copy is innocent:

- `~/.daemonkit/tools/capt-hook/12.20.9/capt-hook/lib/python3.13/site-packages/spawnllm` has **no** wasmtime import anywhere, and its dist metadata does not declare wasmtime.
- `wasmtime` is not installed in that venv at all.

So this is not a missing-dependency bug in the installed package. It is the working tree winning the import, because the hook runs with `--cwd /Users/yasyf/Code/spawnllm` (visible in the `capt-hookd run --event ... --cwd /Users/yasyf/Code/spawnllm` process arguments) and the CWD lands on `sys.path`. The local tree's `_core` requires `wasmtime`, which the capt-hook venv has no reason to carry.

The trigger is incidental: any hook calling `call_cli` inside that repo fails. Here it is the codex plugin's `agent_inject`, whose own source is blameless — byte-identical between the cached 1.5.0 copy and cc-skills main, and it references wasmtime nowhere.

## Why it matters

`call_cli` is a core context helper — `ContextAPI.git` routes through it too, so the blast radius is any hook doing git or CLI work. The failure is a hard `ModuleNotFoundError` propagating out through `run_handler`, logged as `hook handler failed`, rather than a degraded no-op. A user working in a repo that happens to share a name with one of captain_hook's dependencies gets a stream of failing hooks with a traceback pointing at their own source tree, which reads as their bug rather than an import-resolution accident.

The collision surface is wider than one package: any top-level name captain_hook imports lazily is exposed the same way, and the odds are high precisely in the fleet's own repos, since captain_hook depends on fleet packages that are also checked out locally.

## Suggested fix

1. Isolate the interpreter path for hook execution so captain_hook's own imports resolve against its venv — drop CWD/project-dir from `sys.path` for the dispatch process (`-P` / `PYTHONSAFEPATH`, or an explicit `sys.path` scrub before user code runs).
2. Failing that, resolve `run_cli` eagerly at package import time, before any project dir is on the path, rather than lazily inside `call_cli`.
3. Either way, make a failed lazy import inside `call_cli` degrade rather than raise — it already swallows `OSError`/`SubprocessError` under `throw=False`, and `ImportError` belongs in that same class. The codex caller passes `throw=False` and still ate a hard crash.

## Not filed against

- **cc-skills / codex plugin** — the hook is only the trigger; its source has no wasmtime reference on cached 1.5.0 or on main (149d28d).
- **spawnllm** — its local tree is entitled to require wasmtime; nothing should have been importing that tree from inside the capt-hook venv.

ops.text: call_cli imports its dependencies from captain_hook's own venv regardless of the session CWD or project dir
A hook firing in a repo whose top-level package name collides with a captain_hook dependency does not raise ModuleNotFoundError
A shadowed or broken lazy import in call_cli degrades the hook instead of raising through run_handler
